summary: The sons of Israel take their tools to be sharpened. Psalm 7 speaks of a sharpened sword, while Psalm 52 compares a deceitful tongue to a razor with a keen edge.

stems.gloss: work or sharpen a metal edge

senses.definition: Israelites bring agricultural tools to a smith to have their edges sharpened. Psalm 7 uses the same verb for a sword. Job describes an enemy fixing a sharp gaze on him.
A deceitful tongue is compared to a sharpened razor. The danger lies in what its words can do.
The Letushites are named with two other groups among the descendants of Dedan, in the line of Abraham through Keturah. The genealogy gives no meaning for the name.

evidence.locator: s.v. לְטֵשׁ, Targum Genesis 4:22 and Targum Proverbs 27:17

note: The ethnic name resembles the verb but the text gives no account of its origin. The night word already belongs to layil. The creature לִילִית has a different consonantal spelling and its own Akkadian comparison.
